questions.q: In Christian teaching, what does it mean to undergo true 'Repentance'?
options: Feeling sorry about a mistake without intending to change
Paying money to a priest for a pardon
Having a genuine change of heart and mind that leads to turning away from sin
Hiding a bad deed so no one finds out
questions.explain: **Repentance** involves a deep, genuine sorrow for sin coupled with a deliberate decision to turn away from that sin and seek God's forgiveness.

questions.q: Which prophet did God send to King David to confront him and call him to repentance over his sin with Bathsheba? (2 Samuel 12)
options: Elijah
Nathan
Samuel
Isaiah
questions.explain: God sent the prophet **Nathan** to King David. Nathan used a parable about a rich man and a poor man's lamb to convict David of his sin.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: How did King David demonstrate his obedience to God's call to repentance after he was confronted by the prophet?
options: He ordered the prophet to be executed.
He denied doing anything wrong.
He confessed immediately, saying, 'I have sinned against the LORD.'
He blamed Bathsheba for tempting him.
questions.explain: Unlike some other leaders, David immediately admitted his guilt. In **2 Samuel 12:13**, David said to Nathan, 'I have sinned against the LORD.'
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In Jonah 3:1-10, God called the inhabitants of a wicked city to repentance. What was the name of this city?
options: Sodom
Gomorrah
Babylon
Nineveh
questions.explain: God sent Jonah to the great city of **Nineveh** to proclaim that it would be overthrown in forty days because of their wickedness.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: How did the people and the king of Nineveh react to God's message of impending destruction?
options: They mocked the prophet and threw him in prison.
They believed God, proclaimed a fast, put on sackcloth, and turned from their evil ways.
They decided to migrate to another land.
They started a war against Israel.
questions.explain: **Jonah 3:5-8** records that the people of Nineveh **believed God; they called for a fast and put on sackcloth**, and the king ordered everyone to turn from their evil ways.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the New Testament, who was the forerunner that came in the wilderness, urgently calling people to a 'baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins'? (Luke 3:1-3)
options: Apostle Peter
John the Baptist
Nicodemus
Joseph of Arimathea
questions.explain: **John the Baptist** appeared in the wilderness preaching a baptism of repentance to prepare the way for Jesus Christ.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: To show the practical nature of true repentance, what specific instruction did John the Baptist give to the tax collectors? (Luke 3:12-13)
options: To stop paying taxes to the Roman Emperor
To collect no more than what they were authorized to do
To quit their jobs and become fishermen
To divide their wealth equally among the poor
questions.explain: In **Luke 3:13**, when the tax collectors asked what they should do, John told them, '**Collect no more than you are authorized to do**,' indicating that true repentance changes ethical behavior.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: What severe consequence did King Saul face in 1 Samuel because of his continued disobedience and lack of genuine repentance?
options: He was struck with leprosy for the rest of his life.
God rejected him from being king, and the Spirit of the LORD departed from him.
He was swallowed by the earth alive.
He was exiled to Egypt and became a slave.
questions.explain: Because Saul made excuses instead of showing genuine repentance for disobeying God's command, Samuel declared that **God had rejected him from being king** (1 Samuel 15:23), and the Spirit of the Lord departed from him (1 Samuel 16:14).
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: What does a lack of repentance generally result in, according to biblical accounts?
options: Continuous spiritual growth and peace
Separation from God's presence, loss of divine favor, and eventual judgment
An immediate promotion in earthly status
Exemption from keeping God's laws
questions.explain: Throughout the Bible, a lack of repentance (unconfessed and forsaken sin) leads to **separation from God, the removal of His blessings, and judgment**, as seen in the lives of King Saul and others.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: Old Testament (Paper 1)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: According to Mark 1:14-15, Jesus began His public ministry with a strong call for repentance. What were His exact words summarizing this call?
options: The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand; repent and believe in the gospel.
Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets.
Take up your cross and follow me to Jerusalem.
questions.explain: **Mark 1:15** records Jesus saying: '**The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand; repent and believe in the gospel.**'
